questions.question: The residue of \(f(z) = \dfrac{1}{z^2(z-1)}\) at \(z = 0\) is
questions.explanation: Expand \(f(z)\) around \(z=0\). Write \(\frac{1}{z-1} = -(1+z+z^2+\cdots)\), so \(f(z) = -z^{-2}(1+z+z^2+\cdots)\). The coefficient of \(z^{-1}\) (the residue) is \(-1\).

questions.question: The value of the contour integral \(\displaystyle\oint \frac{e^z}{z - i\pi}\,dz\) over the circle \(|z| = 4\) (counterclockwise) is
questions.explanation: By Cauchy's integral formula, the integral \(= 2\pi i \cdot e^{i\pi} = 2\pi i \cdot (-1) = -2\pi i\).

questions.question: Which of the following functions is analytic everywhere in the complex plane (entire)?
questions.explanation: \(e^z\) satisfies the Cauchy–Riemann equations everywhere and is entire. \(1/z\) has a pole at \(z=0\), \(\ln z\) has a branch cut, and \(|z|^2\) fails the CR equations everywhere except \(z=0\).

questions.question: The number of zeros of \(f(z) = z^5 + 3z + 1\) inside the circle \(|z| = 2\) is
questions.explanation: By Rouché's theorem on \(|z|=2\): \(|z^5| = 32\) while \(|3z+1| \leq 7\). So \(f(z)\) has the same number of zeros as \(z^5\), which is \(5\).

questions.question: The Laurent series of \(f(z) = \dfrac{1}{z(z-1)}\) valid for \(0 < |z| < 1\) is
questions.explanation: Partial fractions: \(\frac{1}{z(z-1)} = -\frac{1}{z} + \frac{1}{z-1}\). For \(|z|<1\): \(\frac{1}{z-1} = -\frac{1}{1-z} = -(1+z+z^2+\cdots)\). So \(f(z) = -\frac{1}{z} - 1 - z - z^2 - \cdots\)

questions.question: If \(A\) is a \(3\times3\) matrix with eigenvalues \(1,\,2,\,3\), the trace of \(A^2\) is
The matrix \(A = \begin{pmatrix}0 & 1\\-1 & 0\end{pmatrix}\) represents a rotation by angle \(\theta\). The value of \(\theta\) is
questions.explanation: A rotation matrix is \(\begin{pmatrix}\cos\theta & -\sin\theta\\ \sin\theta & \cos\theta\end{pmatrix}\). Matching entries: \(\cos\theta=0,\;\sin\theta=1 \Rightarrow \theta=\pi/2\).

questions.question: Which of the following statements about a Hermitian matrix is FALSE?
options: Eigenvectors for distinct eigenvalues are orthogonal
It is diagonalisable by a unitary matrix
questions.explanation: A Hermitian matrix can have negative eigenvalues (e.g., \(-I\) is Hermitian with \(\det = (-1)^n < 0\) for odd \(n\)). Statements A, B, and D are all true properties of Hermitian matrices.

questions.question: The rank of the matrix \(\begin{pmatrix}1&2&3\\2&4&6\\3&6&9\end{pmatrix}\) is
questions.explanation: All three rows are multiples of \((1,2,3)\), so there is only one linearly independent row. Hence the rank is \(1\).

questions.question: For the matrix \(A = \begin{pmatrix}2&1\\0&2\end{pmatrix}\), the number of linearly independent eigenvectors is
questions.explanation: \(A\) has a repeated eigenvalue \(\lambda=2\). The matrix \((A-2I)=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\0&0\end{pmatrix}\) has rank 1, so the eigenspace is 1-dimensional — only 1 linearly independent eigenvector.

questions.question: The Fourier transform of \(f(x) = e^{-a|x|}\) \((a>0)\) is
questions.explanation: \(\displaystyle\int_{-\infty}^{\infty} e^{-a|x|}e^{-ikx}dx = \frac{2a}{a^2+k^2}\). Split the integral at \(x=0\) and evaluate each half using standard exponential integrals.

questions.question: The Fourier series of \(f(x) = x\) on \([-\pi,\pi]\) converges at \(x = \pi\) to
questions.explanation: At a jump discontinuity, the Fourier series converges to the average of the left and right limits: \(\dfrac{f(\pi^-)+f(-\pi^+)}{2} = \dfrac{\pi+(-\pi)}{2} = 0\).

questions.question: Parseval's theorem for Fourier transforms states that
questions.explanation: Parseval's theorem: \(\displaystyle\int|f(x)|^2\,dx = \frac{1}{2\pi}\int|F(k)|^2\,dk\), relating the \(L^2\) norm in position and frequency space.

questions.question: The Fourier transform of the Dirac delta function \(\delta(x-a)\) is
questions.explanation: \(\mathcal{F}[\delta(x-a)] = \displaystyle\int_{-\infty}^{\infty} \delta(x-a)\,e^{-ikx}\,dx = e^{-ika}\).

questions.question: The general solution of the ODE \(y'' - 5y' + 6y = 0\) is
questions.explanation: Characteristic equation: \(r^2-5r+6=0 \Rightarrow (r-2)(r-3)=0\), giving \(r=2,\,3\). General solution: \(c_1 e^{2x}+c_2 e^{3x}\).

questions.question: The singular points of the ODE \(x^2y'' + xy' + (x^2-n^2)y = 0\) (Bessel's equation) are
questions.explanation: Dividing by \(x^2\): \(P(x)=1/x\) has a simple pole at \(x=0\) and \(Q(x)=(x^2-n^2)/x^2\) is analytic at \(x=0\) after multiplying by \(x^2\). Hence \(x=0\) is a regular singular point.

questions.question: Using the Frobenius method, the indicial equation for \(xy'' + y' - y = 0\) at \(x=0\) gives the roots
questions.explanation: Here \(p_0=1,\;q_0=0\). The indicial equation is \(r(r-1)+p_0 r+q_0 = r^2 = 0\), giving a double root \(r=0\).

questions.question: The Green's function for \(\dfrac{d^2G}{dx^2} = \delta(x-x')\) on the infinite line with \(G\to 0\) as \(|x|\to\infty\) is
questions.explanation: Integrating \(d^2G/dx^2=\delta(x-x')\) twice and applying the condition \(G\to 0\) at \(|x|\to\infty\) gives \(G = -|x-x'|/2\).

questions.question: The value of the Legendre polynomial \(P_2(\cos\theta)\) is
questions.explanation: \(P_2(x) = \dfrac{3x^2-1}{2}\). Substituting \(x=\cos\theta\) gives \(P_2(\cos\theta) = \dfrac{3\cos^2\theta-1}{2}\).

questions.question: The generating function for Hermite polynomials \(H_n(x)\) is
questions.explanation: The standard generating function is \(e^{2xt-t^2} = \displaystyle\sum_{n=0}^{\infty} H_n(x)\,\frac{t^n}{n!}\).

questions.question: The orthogonality relation for Legendre polynomials is \(\displaystyle\int_{-1}^{1} P_m(x)P_n(x)\,dx =\)
questions.explanation: \(\displaystyle\int_{-1}^{1} P_m(x)P_n(x)\,dx = \frac{2}{2n+1}\,\delta_{mn}\).

questions.question: \(\Gamma\!\left(\tfrac{1}{2}\right)\) is equal to
questions.explanation: \(\Gamma(1/2) = \displaystyle\int_0^\infty t^{-1/2}e^{-t}\,dt = \sqrt{\pi}\), which follows from the Gaussian integral \(\int_{-\infty}^{\infty}e^{-x^2}dx=\sqrt{\pi}\).

questions.question: Which of the following are valid recurrence relations for Bessel functions? (Select all that apply)
questions.image_caption: Bessel functions of the second kind
questions.explanation: Both \(J_{n-1}(x)+J_{n+1}(x)=\frac{2n}{x}J_n(x)\) and \(J_{n-1}(x)-J_{n+1}(x)=2J_n'(x)\) are standard recurrence relations for Bessel functions.

questions.question: The divergence of \(\mathbf{F} = x^2\,\hat{i} + y^2\,\hat{j} + z^2\,\hat{k}\) at the point \((1,1,1)\) is
questions.explanation: \(\nabla\cdot\mathbf{F} = \dfrac{\partial(x^2)}{\partial x}+\dfrac{\partial(y^2)}{\partial y}+\dfrac{\partial(z^2)}{\partial z} = 2x+2y+2z\). At \((1,1,1)\): \(2+2+2=6\).

questions.question: Stokes' theorem relates
options: Volume integral of divergence to surface integral
Line integral around a closed curve to surface integral of curl
Surface integral to volume integral of gradient
questions.explanation: Stokes' theorem: \(\displaystyle\oint_C \mathbf{F}\cdot d\mathbf{r} = \iint_S (\nabla\times\mathbf{F})\cdot d\mathbf{S}\). It connects a line integral around a closed loop to the surface integral of the curl.

questions.question: If \(\varphi = x^2yz\), the gradient \(\nabla\varphi\) at \((1,2,3)\) is
The curl of \(\mathbf{F} = y\,\hat{i} - x\,\hat{j}\) is
questions.explanation: \(\nabla\times\mathbf{F} = \left(\dfrac{\partial(-x)}{\partial x}-\dfrac{\partial y}{\partial y}\right)\hat{k} = (-1-1)\hat{k} = -2\hat{k}\).

questions.question: The order of the group \(S_3\) (symmetric group on 3 elements) is
questions.explanation: \(S_3\) consists of all permutations of 3 elements. The number of permutations is \(3! = 6\).

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a group under matrix multiplication?
options: All \(2\times2\) real matrices including singular ones
questions.explanation: The set of all \(2\times2\) real matrices fails to be a group because singular matrices have no inverse. \(GL(2,\mathbb{R})\), \(SL(2,\mathbb{R})\), and \(O(2)\) are all valid groups.

questions.question: The number of irreducible representations of a finite group equals
options: Half the order of the group
questions.explanation: A fundamental theorem of representation theory states that the number of irreducible representations of a finite group equals its number of conjugacy classes.

questions.question: The group \(\mathbb{Z}_4 = \{0,1,2,3\}\) under addition mod 4 is isomorphic to
questions.explanation: \(\mathbb{Z}_4\) is cyclic of order 4, generated by 1, hence isomorphic to \(C_4\). Note: \(\mathbb{Z}_2\times\mathbb{Z}_2 \cong V_4\) has no element of order 4, so it is not isomorphic to \(\mathbb{Z}_4\).

questions.question: For a Gaussian distribution with mean \(\mu\) and standard deviation \(\sigma\), the probability that a measurement lies within \(\pm2\sigma\) of the mean is approximately
questions.image_caption: Standard deviation intervals of a Gaussian
questions.explanation: The empirical rule: \(\approx 68.3\%\), \(95.4\%\), \(99.7\%\) of data lies within \(\pm1\sigma\), \(\pm2\sigma\), \(\pm3\sigma\) respectively.

questions.question: If \(X\) and \(Y\) are independent random variables each uniformly distributed on \([0,1]\), the PDF of \(Z=X+Y\) at \(z=1\) is
questions.explanation: The PDF of \(Z=X+Y\) is a triangular distribution: \(f_Z(z)=z\) for \(0\leq z\leq1\) and \(2-z\) for \(1<z\leq2\). At \(z=1\): \(f_Z(1)=1\).

questions.question: The characteristic function of a Poisson distribution with parameter \(\lambda\) is
questions.explanation: For Poisson\((\lambda)\): \(\varphi(t) = E[e^{itX}] = \displaystyle\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}e^{itk}\frac{e^{-\lambda}\lambda^k}{k!} = e^{\lambda(e^{it}-1)}\).

questions.question: The trace of a second-rank tensor \(T_{ij}\) (contraction \(T_{ii}\)) transforms as
questions.explanation: Contracting two indices of a rank-2 tensor reduces the rank by 2, yielding a scalar (rank-0 tensor). The trace \(T_{ii}\) is invariant under coordinate transformations.

questions.question: The Levi-Civita symbol \(\varepsilon_{123}\) equals
questions.explanation: \(\varepsilon_{123}=+1\) since \((1,2,3)\) is an even permutation of \((1,2,3)\). In general \(\varepsilon_{ijk}=+1\) for even permutations, \(-1\) for odd, and \(0\) if any two indices repeat.

questions.question: How many independent components does a symmetric traceless tensor of rank 2 in 3D have?
questions.explanation: A symmetric \(3\times3\) tensor has \(6\) independent components. Imposing tracelessness removes 1 constraint, leaving \(6-1=5\) independent components.

questions.question: Under a proper rotation, the dot product \(\mathbf{A}\cdot\mathbf{B}\) of two polar vectors
questions.explanation: The dot product of two proper vectors is a scalar — it is invariant under rotations. This is the defining property of a rank-0 tensor.

questions.question: If \(f(z)=u+iv\) is analytic, which pair satisfies the Cauchy–Riemann equations?
options: \(\dfrac{\partial u}{\partial x}=\dfrac{\partial v}{\partial y}\) and \(\dfrac{\partial u}{\partial y}=\dfrac{\partial v}{\partial x}\)
\(\dfrac{\partial u}{\partial x}=\dfrac{\partial v}{\partial y}\) and \(\dfrac{\partial u}{\partial y}=-\dfrac{\partial v}{\partial x}\)
\(\dfrac{\partial u}{\partial x}=-\dfrac{\partial v}{\partial y}\) and \(\dfrac{\partial u}{\partial y}=\dfrac{\partial v}{\partial x}\)
\(\dfrac{\partial u}{\partial x}=-\dfrac{\partial v}{\partial y}\) and \(\dfrac{\partial u}{\partial y}=-\dfrac{\partial v}{\partial x}\)
questions.explanation: The Cauchy–Riemann equations are: \(\dfrac{\partial u}{\partial x}=\dfrac{\partial v}{\partial y}\) and \(\dfrac{\partial u}{\partial y}=-\dfrac{\partial v}{\partial x}\). These are necessary and sufficient for analyticity.

questions.question: The PDE \(\dfrac{\partial^2 u}{\partial t^2} = c^2\dfrac{\partial^2 u}{\partial x^2}\) (wave equation) is classified as
questions.image_caption: Standing wave solution of the wave equation
questions.explanation: For \(Au_{xx}+Bu_{xt}+Cu_{tt}=f\): \(A=c^2,\,B=0,\,C=-1\). Discriminant \(B^2-4AC = 4c^2 > 0\) → Hyperbolic.

questions.question: The heat equation \(\dfrac{\partial u}{\partial t} = \alpha\dfrac{\partial^2 u}{\partial x^2}\) is classified as
questions.explanation: For the heat equation \(A=\alpha,\,B=0,\,C=0\). Discriminant \(B^2-4AC=0\) → Parabolic.

questions.question: The convolution theorem for Fourier transforms states: \(\mathcal{F}[f*g](k) =\)
questions.explanation: The convolution theorem: \(\mathcal{F}[f*g](k) = F(k)\cdot G(k)\). The Fourier transform converts convolution in position space to pointwise multiplication in frequency space.

questions.question: Which of the following sets of vectors is linearly independent?
questions.explanation: Option C is the standard basis of \(\mathbb{R}^3\) — always linearly independent. Option A: \((1,1,0)=(1,0,0)+(0,1,0)\). Option B: all rows proportional. Option D: check \(\det = 0\) — dependent.

questions.question: The associated Laguerre polynomial \(L^1_1(x)\) equals
questions.explanation: \(L^k_n(x) = (-1)^k \frac{d^k}{dx^k}L_{n+k}(x)\). One finds \(L^1_1(x) = 2-x\).

questions.question: The generators of \(SU(2)\) are related to which physical observable?
questions.explanation: The generators of \(SU(2)\) are the Pauli matrices \(\boldsymbol{\sigma}/2\), which correspond to the spin-\(\frac{1}{2}\) angular momentum operators \(\hat{S}_x,\hat{S}_y,\hat{S}_z\).

questions.question: Cauchy's integral theorem states that \(\oint_C f(z)\,dz = 0\) if
questions.explanation: Cauchy's integral theorem: if \(f(z)\) is analytic (holomorphic) in a simply connected region and \(C\) is any closed contour therein, then \(\oint_C f(z)\,dz=0\).

questions.question: The variance of a binomial distribution \(B(n,p)\) is
questions.explanation: For \(B(n,p)\): mean \(=np\), variance \(=np(1-p)=npq\) where \(q=1-p\).

questions.question: For a scalar field \(\varphi\), which of the following is always zero?
questions.explanation: The curl of a gradient is always zero: \(\nabla\times(\nabla\varphi)=\mathbf{0}\). This is an identity following from Schwarz's theorem on the symmetry of mixed partial derivatives.

questions.question: The Laplace transform of \(f(t)=t^n\) is
questions.explanation: \(\mathcal{L}\{t^n\} = \displaystyle\int_0^\infty t^n e^{-st}\,dt = \dfrac{\Gamma(n+1)}{s^{n+1}} = \dfrac{n!}{s^{n+1}}\) for non-negative integer \(n\).

questions.question: A Sturm–Liouville problem \([p(x)y']' + [q(x)+\lambda w(x)]y=0\) has eigenvalues that are
questions.explanation: The Sturm–Liouville theorem guarantees real eigenvalues forming an infinite discrete sequence \(\lambda_1<\lambda_2<\lambda_3<\cdots\to\infty\), with corresponding orthogonal eigenfunctions.

questions.question: The Möbius transformation \(w = \dfrac{z-i}{z+i}\) maps the upper half-plane \(\text{Im}(z)>0\) to
options: The exterior of the unit circle
questions.explanation: The Möbius transformation \(w=(z-i)/(z+i)\) is a classical map from the upper half-plane to the open unit disk \(|w|<1\), sending \(z=0\mapsto -1\), \(z=i\mapsto 0\), \(z\to\infty\mapsto 1\).

questions.question: The characteristic polynomial of \(A=\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\0&1\end{pmatrix}\) is
questions.explanation: \(\det(A-\lambda I) = \det\begin{pmatrix}1-\lambda&1\\0&1-\lambda\end{pmatrix} = (1-\lambda)^2 = 0\).

questions.question: A representation of a group is called irreducible if
options: It cannot be decomposed into smaller invariant subspace representations
questions.explanation: An irreducible representation (irrep) has no proper invariant subspace — it cannot be brought to block-diagonal form by any similarity transformation.

questions.question: The Dirac delta function satisfies \(\delta(ax) =\)
questions.explanation: Under scaling: \(\delta(ax) = \delta(x)/|a|\). This follows from \(\displaystyle\int\delta(ax)f(x)\,dx = f(0)/|a| = \int(\delta(x)/|a|)f(x)\,dx\).

questions.question: Which boundary condition makes the Laplacian \(\nabla^2\) self-adjoint on a finite domain?
options: Neumann: \(\partial u/\partial n=0\) on the boundary
questions.explanation: The Laplacian is self-adjoint under both Dirichlet (\(u=0\)) and Neumann (\(\partial u/\partial n=0\)) boundary conditions, since in both cases the boundary term in Green's second identity vanishes.

questions.question: The divergence theorem (Gauss's theorem) states that \(\displaystyle\oiint_S \mathbf{F}\cdot d\mathbf{A} =\)
questions.image_caption: Flux through a closed surface equals volume integral of divergence
questions.explanation: Gauss's divergence theorem: \(\displaystyle\oiint_S \mathbf{F}\cdot d\mathbf{A} = \iiint_V (\nabla\cdot\mathbf{F})\,dV\). It converts a closed surface integral into a volume integral of the divergence.

questions.question: Bayes' theorem states \(P(A|B) =\)
questions.explanation: Bayes' theorem: \(P(A|B) = \dfrac{P(B|A)\,P(A)}{P(B)}\). It describes how to update a prior probability \(P(A)\) given new evidence \(B\).

questions.question: The Kronecker delta \(\delta_{ij}\) acts as the metric tensor in
options: Flat Euclidean space with Cartesian coordinates
questions.explanation: In flat Euclidean space with Cartesian coordinates, the metric tensor is simply \(\delta_{ij}\): \(ds^2 = \delta_{ij}\,dx^i\,dx^j = dx^2+dy^2+dz^2\).

questions.question: The function \(f(z) = \bar{z}\) (complex conjugate) is
questions.explanation: Writing \(f(z)=x-iy\): the Cauchy–Riemann check gives \(\partial u/\partial x=1\neq \partial v/\partial y=-1\). The equations are never satisfied, so \(f(z)=\bar{z}\) is analytic nowhere.

questions.question: The inverse Laplace transform of \(F(s) = \dfrac{1}{s^2+\omega^2}\) is
questions.explanation: \(\mathcal{L}\left\{\dfrac{\sin(\omega t)}{\omega}\right\} = \dfrac{1}{s^2+\omega^2}\). Therefore \(\mathcal{L}^{-1}\!\left\{\dfrac{1}{s^2+\omega^2}\right\} = \dfrac{\sin(\omega t)}{\omega}\).
